head: ṭbx (< Arab. ṭbx cf. Wehr 763: kochen;)

examples.turoyo: aṯi bazərgān, maḥatle gabe w ṭbəxle l-u=bazərgān muklo
examples.translation: dahin kam ein Kaufmann, stieg in seiner Nähe ab und kochte sein Essen
examples.raw: aṯi bazərgān, maḥatle gabe w ṭbəxle l-u=bazərgān muklo ʻdahin kam ein Kaufmann, stieg in seiner Nähe ab und kochte sein Essenʼ; 68; prs 49/30;

examples.turoyo: deri yawmo ṭbəxla ḥamuṣo “mə ṭbəxlax?” ummo “ašər, ṭbəxli ḥamuṣo” “qay lo=ṭbəxlax ḥalyo?” mḥéle-la
examples.translation: The next day she cooked sour [food]. “What have you cooked?” She says “I have cooked sour [food]” “Why have not you cooked sweet [food]?” [And] he hit her
examples.raw: deri yawmo ṭbəxla ḥamuṣo “mə ṭbəxlax?” ummo “ašər, ṭbəxli ḥamuṣo” “qay lo=ṭbəxlax ḥalyo?” mḥéle-la ‘The next day she cooked sour [food]. “What have you cooked?” She says “I have cooked sour [food]” “Why have not you cooked sweet [food]?” [And] he hit her’; 41/9

examples.translation: der Knabe kochte (also) für den Onkel
examples.raw: u=kurrəko ko-ṭobəx l-u=ḥolo ʻder Knabe kochte (also) für den Onkelʼ; 99; 69/308;

examples.translation: I cook sweet [food] – he beats me; [I cook] sour [food] – he [also] beats me
examples.raw: ṭubxono ḥalyo, ko-moḥe-li; ḥamuṣo ko-moḥe-li ‘I cook sweet [food] – he beats me; [I cook] sour [food] – he [also] beats me’; 41/17
